scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Exact Uniform Sampling of Contingency Tables with Arbitrary Margins” (preprints/Exact-Uniform-Sampling-of-Contingency-Tables-with-Arbitrary-Margins-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 115 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 be1d677ab515ceb2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For arbitrary nonnegative integer margins of equal total, the following algorithms exist in the model of unbiased random bits and bit operations. (i) Given an integer k ≥ 1, a bounded-time algorithm outputs a table in Ω(r, c) whose law is within 2−k in total variation of the uniform law. Its running time is polynomial in m, n, log(N +1), k. (ii) An algorithm outputs an exactly uniform table in Ω(r, c), terminates almost surely, and has expected running time polynomial in m, n, log(N + 1). The polynomials are uniform over all margin vectors. No positivity, sparsity, balance, or fixed- dimension hypothesis is imposed.
